Defense lens

How to read this

Higher points allowed can indicate a favorable fantasy matchup, but this is a historical signal—not a future opponent projection.

What is measured?
All fantasy points scored by players at the selected position against each defense, divided by distinct team-game matchups in the available data.
What comes next?
Upcoming schedule, injuries, projections, and lineup optimization require new data feeds. We’ll add them as separate modules.

The highly scientific Lazar-Finkle formula

For entertainment only. Each player's Trade Score combines 60% season fantasy points/game, 30% last-three-games average, and 10% season-low points/game. Scores are added across all players on each side; recent games can be noisy. This is not a rest-of-season forecast and does not account for injuries, schedule, roster needs, keeper value, or the value of open roster spots. Cross-position comparisons may be misleading.

Source: nflverse stats_player • regular season only • historical data • no live projections.
Built for analysis and education. Fantasy-point calculations follow the imported dataset and may differ from individual league scoring. Data: nflverse. Published GitHub Pages versions attempt to refresh from data/player_weekly_master.csv; embedded records provide an offline fallback.
